newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Tuesday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Tuesday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Tuesday:

Spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said reports that the Commission's inquiry into the merger of Boeing Co. and McDonnell Douglas Corp. was politically motivated were not acceptable. He said the Commission would take its final decision on July 31, not before.
Commissioner Karel Van Miert expects to send a statement of objections before the end of May, van der Pas added.

In answer to a question on the Commission's intentions regarding Internet voice telephony, spokesman Willy Helin said it would not put the service providers into a straightjacket but it wanted the conditions regulating this market to be flexible and adaptable to the constant evolution in technology.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/395: Victims of war in Chechnya: European Commission approves humanitarian aid worth ECU 1.4 million.
- IP/97/396: Worker Involvement: Davignon Group Final Report.
- IP/97/398: Commission clears the creation of a joint venture in the consumer credit sector.
- IP/97/399: Telephony on the Internet: Commission asks interested parties for comments.
- IP/97/400: "Our analysis of the Boeing-McDonnell Douglas file is conducted strictly on the basis of the European merger regulation, and nothing else" Mr Karel Van Miert says.
- Speech/97/108: Commissioner Christos Papoutsis at first meeting of the Euro-Mediterranean Energy Forum.
- Eurostat Memo No 4/97: Where in Europe do 60% of men marry foreign women?
